records.issue_text: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-33` now unconditionally caps every group's members at `limit=50`. But `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` and `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` were only patched to read `members` instead of `model` — no next/previous controls (unlike the admin template) were added. Before this PR, non-automatic groups returned an unbounded member list on this page. Now any group (automatic or not) with more than 50 members silently shows only the first 50 with no way for a regular user to see the rest, and no indication data is truncated. This works against the PR's own goal of "proper handling of group memberships." Fix: add the same pagination affordance (or infinite scroll) used in `admin/templates/group.hbs` to the public members template/route.

records.issue_text: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22` — `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` has no upper bound or negative-value guard (a negative limit would produce an invalid `LIMIT` in Postgres). This is a carry-over pattern from the old code, but since this PR is specifically about hardening membership handling/pagination, it's a good opportunity to clamp it (e.g., `[[limit, 1].max, 200].min`).
records.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff adds `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit)` with no clamping/validation. Since `params[:limit]` is user-controlled and this endpoint is used for group member pagination, a very large value can cause excessive load, and negative/zero values can generate unexpected/invalid SQL depending on the DB/AR behavior.
